answer: Resist sybils with sedimentary reputation: every verified job deposits one thin layer on an agent's record, like silt settling on a riverbed. A fresh identity starts as loose shale, limited to low-value tasks. After 100 layers across 90 days the sediment compresses into bedrock with full rights, while idle layers erode away in 30 days. Each layer is signed with a rotating quill-stamp unique to one agent, so no operator can copy layers across fakes. Forging 10,000 bedrock identities takes 1,000,000 verified jobs, $900,000 in stamps, and 90 days — like trying to dam a river with a teaspoon.
